channel.title: Chovy's Blog
channel.description: Tech, agentic coding, and whatever else I'm building. By Anthony "chovy" Ettinger.

item.title: Why I wrote hqtui
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Every TypeScript terminal UI library is either abandoned since 2015, a React flexbox layout engine, or a native binary behind FFI. I wanted btop quality with zero dependencies, so I wrote hqtui.

item.title: Why I built DiskPush
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: FileZilla re-uploads a folder because one file changed; rsync does not, but it means remembering the flags. I wanted the two pane browser on top of the rsync engine, could not find it, so we built it.

item.title: I cloned myself at chovy.com
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: chovy.com went from a 240-character microblog to an AI clone of me: a four-line advisor persona, an isolated coding worker on its own service, and a roster where human teammates and AI workers are counted separately.

item.title: Four days at Lake Almanor
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Four days off the computer at Lake Almanor with two friends from high school. The backpack with all the warez stayed home, so the dispensary in Westwood and the smoke shop in Chester restocked the trip in one afternoon.

item.title: Cards and crypto in one checkout
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: One API call returns a Polygon address and a live Stripe Checkout session. Putting both rails behind one page, the bug that meant the card tab never rendered, and what ten days of realtime fraud screening actually logged.

item.title: I listed a GitHub App before building the backend
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: ThreatCrush has a GitHub App listing now. The app asks for two read permissions and nothing else, on purpose, because widening a published listing is harder than starting narrow. Plus the setup URL that 404d on every installer, and how to tell a draft Marketplace listing from a typo.

item.title: Four genres, and the filter that was eating the other 89%
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: The music section of my release-tracker listed four genres. I blamed the data source. The data source was fine: my own ingest was dropping nine out of every ten releases, and the fix was already sitting in the schema.

item.title: A dead A record and six modules that never loaded
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: A subdomain pointed at a VPS that no longer exists, and nothing was watching it. Fixing it surfaced six modules failing silently behind a green health check, plus a runtime that loaded one more module than the other.

item.title: What each feature actually costs me in AI
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Five agents, five git worktrees, one command that reads the engines' own logs. Over 90 percent of a $228 day turned out to be cache reads, and a bug hunt cost 65 times what a short blog session did.

item.title: Our customers block ads, so we sell them in the terminal
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Every product we ship is aimed at developers, and developers are the hardest audience on earth to buy. So we built the one ad format nobody else sells: a plain text unit you curl into an MOTD.
